newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl "very satisfied" with tax reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Kohl "very satisfied" with tax reform plan.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he was happy with the tax reform plan put together by coalition finance experts on Wednesday.
Speaking ahead of a meeting of leaders from his Christian Democrat party (CDU), Kohl said "I am very satisfied".

A coalition tax policy working group chaired by Finance Minister Theo Waigel agreed on a plan to slash income taxes and broaden the tax base in a two-year reform which would leave Germans 30 billion marks better off at the end of the day.
The group, however, left open the question of increasing value-added tax to partly finance the cuts in direct taxation.
Kohl's CDU is split on the VAT issue. Young regional leaders oppose to an increase, but a majority at party headquarters wants a two-point rise to help bail out Germany's welfare system.
The three parties in Kohl's coalition were discussing the reform plan separately ahead of its unveiling by Waigel later.
